Dear all,

 

I‘m currently trying to submit an article to a journal where text in graphs has to be in Times New Roman, font size 9pt, when squeezed into the width of a column of 84mm. I would be most grateful if anybody could help me please. Unfortunately, I have prepared my graphs, one of which I attached as a PDF, without any set dimensions. I have tried to find out how to change font type and size in grid.text, and how to define the width of the plot, but wasn’t successful. I have attached the same graph as an R-script as well but if someone wants to have a brief look at my current problem I also pasted it in below.

 

Best wishes and many thanks in advance,

 

Martin

 

 

rm(list=ls())

 

library(proto)

library(grid)

library(reshape)

library(plyr)

library(digest)

library(ggplot2)

 

 

df.perc.2 <- structure(list(trt = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L), class = "factor", .Label = c("0-1", "1-2", "2-3")),

                resp = c(100, 94.0193416337148, 90.4454585871723,

                               100, 97.865467535666, 95.8563947267053),

                group = structure(c(2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("eggs in worker cells", "eggs in drone cells"), class = "factor"),

                se = c(0, 1.68994661360938, 2.95728999211006,

                               0, 0.549126551165786, 0.824844616926236)),

                .Names = c("trt", "resp", "group", "se"), row.names = c(NA, -6L), class = "data.frame")

 

 

# Currently, I'm saving plots in this way. However, I'm open for better suggestions:

 

# pdf("C:\\Users\\mhk\\Documents\\nur.fueR\\cost of worker policing project analysis_part 1\\Graphiken in ggplot2\\PDFs, PNGs\\A.plot5h.pdf")

                scale_colour_manual(values = c("#000000", "#000000")) +

                geom_smooth(aes(ymax = resp + se, ymin = resp - se), data = df.perc.2, stat = "identity", size = 1) +

                opts(legend.position = c(0.38, 0.313), legend.background = theme_rect(colour = 0)) +

grid.draw(editGrob(g, gPath( "text"), grep=TRUE,global=TRUE,
gp=gpar(fontfamily="Times")))
dev.off()


HTH,

baptiste

Hi Martin:

You may need to play with this a little, but this seems to work in principle for me.

df <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 2 + 0.5 * (1:10) + rnorm(10, 0, 0.4))
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_smooth(size = 1) +
   opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 16)) +
   opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 16)) +
   opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20)) +
   opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle = 90))
ggsave('testGraph.pdf', height = 3.3, width = 3.3, family = 'Times',
         pointsize = 9, useDingbats = FALSE)

HTH,
Dennis
